sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 7980 of 2023
Applicant :- Dinesh Kumar
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Civil Secrt. Home Depptt. Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjeev Dwivedi,Avnish Kumar Tiwari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.

In terms of the FIR, it was alleged by the informant that on 16.03.2023 at about 5 AM in the morning when the victim had gone to relieve herself, the applicant came and started misbehaving with her and touching her inappropriately.
On her raising hue and cry, two persons saved her.
Similar statement was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., however, in the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim alleged the commission of rape.

sentences.text: 3. The counsel for the applicant argues that the victim has refused to undergo medical examination as is clear from C.A.-1 annexed along with the counter affidavit.
Admittedly the victim is the wife and married lady aged about 30 years.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the huge variance in the FIR, statements under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. coupled with the fact that the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is not supported by any document, the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 17.04.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Dinesh Kumar be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.122 of 2023, under Sections 354, 376, 506 IPC, Police Station Pali, District Hardoi, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 17.1.2024 Arun  Dinesh Kumar vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Civil ... on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54508755/
